subject: Hosted API: sudden p95/p99 latency increase — egress path mismatch
messages:
From: Jorge Perez <jorge.perez@cloudline-sys.com>

Cc: ops@cloudline-sys.com

Subject: [URGENT] 2027-05-02 spike: p95/p99 latency increase for our org

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

We're seeing a large jump in p95/p99 RTT for requests to the Hosted API for our org (org_id: cl-9873). The dashboard shows p95 up from ~120ms to ~380ms and p99 approaching 1.2s starting ~08:45 PDT. Error rate is also slightly elevated (4xx throttle-like). This started suddenly and is impacting production.

Attached: short trace file and a screenshot of the latency chart.

Can you confirm whether there were any routing or regional changes today? We have clients in US-W and are seeing requests get slow — looks like cross-region RTT.

--

Date: 2027-05-02T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] 2027-05-02 spike: p95/p99 latency increase for our org

Rafael / Marissa — initial quick triage below.

Summary (prelim):
- We observed the same p95/p99 jump in our internal monitoring starting 08:40 PDT.
- Error rate (4xx) is correlated with a small surge of cross-region egress for Cloudline's org.
- Trace sample (from Jorge) shows many requests with RTT spikes where the upstream hop indicates eu-central-1 as the selected egress region.

Root cause hypothesis: an egress-mapping rule that ties org_id -> prefer-region was incorrectly updated in route-orchestrator (route-orch) config during a recent deploy; Cloudline's traffic started being steered to EU nodes instead of US-W which explains ~300-600ms extra RTT for many requests.

Immediate mitigation attempted (09:32):
- Reverted the recent route-orch rollout for the affected feature flag for mapping precedence (flag: egress-pref-prio).
- Placed a temporary override mapping to force cl-9873 to us-west-2.

Observed result: p95 dropped to ~160ms within two minutes after override; p99 reduced but still slightly elevated (we're continuing to flush caches and ensure KV propagation). Error rate trending down.

Next steps (short):
- Keep the override active while we perform a controlled fix in route-orch and validate map propagation.
- Run a targeted test sweep for cl-9873 across regional ingress points.
- Postmortem + config audit to follow.

Attachments: support-log-snippet.txt (routing logs), quick excerpt of the trace.

- Engineering will run a propagation audit and provide a postmortem within 72 hours.
- As a gesture for the impact, we'd like to offer a one-time service credit; Rafael will coordinate the amount with you.

Subject: Fwd: [URGENT] 2027-05-02 spike: p95/p99 latency increase for our org — execs: credit approval + SLA note

Sean — FYI and ask. Cloudline (prospect-turned-customer, CL-2026-091) experienced a routing misconfiguration that routed traffic to eu-central causing p95/p99 spikes. Hannah's team applied an override and numbers improved rapidly.

Requested approvals:
- One-time service credit up to $12,500 USD to make Cloudline whole for impacted window (they lost real user transactions).
- We should pre-approve a short SLA exception (reduced latency SLO for the 08:40–09:05 window) for bookkeeping.

Diego and Hannah are preparing the postmortem and configuration diff; I'll route it to legal/finance if you OK the credit.

Short summary for execs: root cause = route-orch mapping precedence regression after deploy; immediate fix = override + rollback of mapping rollout; impact = elevated p95/p99 and small 4xx uptick for Cloudline's org.

Rafael

Please share the postmortem and the configuration change set when available (we'll need it for our compliance review). We confirmed the majority of impacted requests were routed via eu-central-1 incorrectly — your summary matches our findings.

We'll schedule the 14:00 PDT sync tomorrow for a technical review.
